title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Ivanti Connect Secure
text: Multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in Ivanti Connect Secure which could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands and escalate privileges to root on the targeted appliance. Software Affected: Ivanti Connect Secure versions prior to 25.1.3.0; Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2 through 22.8R2.4. Versions 22.7R2.14 and earlier are not affected. Description: An authentication bypass by spoofing (CVE-2026-104935) allows remote command execution; a missing authentication for a critical function (CVE-2026-111357) allows privilege escalation. These vulnerabilities are being exploited in the wild. Solution: Apply the vendor updates 22.8R2.5 or 25.1.3.0 and perform integrity checks of the appliance.

title: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN
text: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability has been reported in the SSL-VPN component of Fortinet FortiOS which could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP requests. CVE identifier is awaited. Software Affected: FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.8 and FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.4. The vendor is aware of reports of limited exploitation in the wild. Solution: Upgrade to FortiOS 7.2.9, 7.4.5 or later. As a workaround, disable SSL-VPN.

title: Credential Phishing Campaign Targeting Indian Banking Customers
text: An active phishing campaign is impersonating Indian banks to harvest net-banking credentials and one-time passwords. Victims receive SMS messages with links to lookalike domains such as navnidhi-bank-secure[.]example and suvarnarekha-kyc-update[.]example hosted on 198.51.100.77. The landing pages deliver an Android banking trojan from hxxp://navnidhi-bank-secure[.]example/kyc.apk (SHA-256 4f8d2c1e9b7a6d5c3e2f1a0b9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d). Banks should block these indicators, alert customers and monitor for account takeover.

title: Vulnerability in Siemens SIMATIC WinCC
text: A vulnerability has been reported in Siemens SIMATIC WinCC which could allow an attacker with network access to the operator station to bypass authentication of the WinCC runtime and manipulate process visualisation. Software Affected: SIMATIC WinCC versions before 8.0 Update 3. Critical infrastructure operators in the energy and transport sectors are advised to restrict network access to operator stations and apply the update.
